rows.explanation: The verse joins the saints’ endurance with keeping God’s commandments and faith in Jesus, echoing patience, righteous action, and faith.
The verse says that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone, closely joining faith with deeds.
The verse urges believers to spur one another toward love and good works, matching the ayah’s mutual encouragement to righteous action.
The verse describes believers as full of goodness and knowledge, able to admonish one another, joining good conduct with mutual counsel.
The verse tells the community to warn, comfort, and support one another and to be patient toward all, echoing mutual counsel and patience.
The verse commands people to speak truth to their neighbors and uphold truth in their community, matching the mutual counsel to truth.
The verse says Paul and Barnabas exhorted the disciples to continue in faith and endure tribulation on the way to God’s kingdom.
The verse commends works, service, faith, and patience, echoing several of the qualities named in the ayah.
The verse urges believers not to grow weary in doing good, joining righteous action with perseverance.
The verse tells believers to exhort one another, matching the ayah’s reciprocal encouragement.
The verse describes the upright person as doing righteousness and speaking truth, joining righteous conduct with truth.
The verse pairs trust in the Lord with doing good, echoing faith and righteous action.
The verse commands preaching, reproof, and exhortation with patience, joining counsel grounded in teaching with endurance.
The verse commands believers to bear one another’s burdens, depicting mutual support in hardship.
The verse tells believers to pursue what is good for one another and for all, echoing communal commitment to good.
The verse describes those who reject the truth and take pleasure in unrighteousness, reversing faithfulness to truth and righteous action.
The verse depicts the fool denying God and doing abominable deeds, opposing belief and good action.
The verse condemns loving evil over good and lies over righteousness, reversing the ayah’s orientation toward good and truth.
The verse describes people suppressing the truth through unrighteousness, opposing its call to hold to truth and do what is right.
The verse describes hearers who hold fast to the word and bear fruit with patience, joining reception of the message, good action, and endurance.
The verse pairs work of faith and labor of love with patience of hope, echoing faith, deeds, and endurance.
The verse says that those who believe in God should be careful to maintain good works, joining belief with righteous action.
The verse urges pursuit of righteousness, faith, love, and peace alongside others who call on the Lord.
The verse commands believers to exhort one another daily so none is hardened by sin’s deceitfulness into unbelief.
The verse calls believers to teach and admonish one another through the word of Christ.
The verse describes speaking the truth in love so the whole body may grow.
The verse urges longsuffering and forbearance with one another, echoing patience within a community.
The verse promises life to those who patiently continue in well-doing.
The verse commends the believers’ patience and faith amid persecutions and tribulations.
The verse commends those who do good and bear suffering patiently.
The verse says that the testing of faith produces patience.
The verse names the patience and faith of the saints.
The verse presents a friend’s faithful rebuke as trustworthy counsel.
The verse says people deceive their neighbors and do not speak truth, reversing mutual counsel in truth.
The verse describes those who disobey the truth and obey unrighteousness, reversing truth and righteous action.
The verse describes people who resist the truth and are reprobate concerning the faith.
The verse says that one who does not do righteousness or love a brother is not of God, reversing righteous action and care within the community.
The verse calls a person who claims to know God but does not keep his commandments a liar without the truth.
The verse describes evildoers avoiding the light because they do not want their deeds exposed.
The verse portrays truth fallen in the street and justice turned away, depicting the collapse of truth in public life.
